title: Microsoft 365 admin center: Copilot Chat usage report for GCC, GCC High and DoD
summary: The roadmap facts, report metrics, privacy control and Graph call are supported. Two minor clarifications remain: the general entry-point list is not government-cloud availability guidance, and the overview explicitly defers reporting-period details to the individual report article.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the government-cloud report appears automatically or requires an enabling action.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Chat usage report" automatically enabled default GCC rollout; "Copilot Chat usage report" "GCC" enable report. Read the report article, usage reports overview and Copilot overview; none specifies an automatic-arrival default or an enabling action for this report.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not named a licence required to view this report, and the report article lists none.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Chat usage report" "license" viewing report subscription; Microsoft 365 admin center usage reports licensing prerequisites Copilot Chat report included subscription plans. Read report, reports overview, Copilot overview and licence options; found no named report-viewing licence.

claims.claim: The concealment control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote: select Settings ... Select Org Settings. ... On the Services tab, select Reports. ... In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings updates the tenant's report settings.
claims.quote: Update tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports. ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/reportSettings

claims.claim: Global administrators can change the setting to display concealed information.
claims.quote: Global administrators can update the settings to display concealed information if your organization's privacy practices allow it.

claims.claim: The request-body property that sets concealment is displayConcealedNames.
claims.quote: The following table specifies the properties that can be updated. ... displayConcealedNames | Boolean

claims.claim: Setting displayConcealedNames to false shows identifiable information.
claims.quote: If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.claim: The printed Graph call uses the beta API.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/reportSettings

claims.where: controls[0].scope, note; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The concealment choice is tenant-wide and applies to usage reports generally rather than only Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Update tenant-level settings for Microsoft 365 reports. ... If set to true, all reports conceal user information such as usernames, groups, and sites. If false, all reports show identifiable information.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The report provides insights into active usage of Microsoft Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Copilot Chat usage report provides insights into active usage of Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The report includes active users.
claims.quote: Active users shows the total number of users who submitted at least one prompt to Microsoft Copilot Chat during the selected period.

claims.claim: The report includes average daily active users.
claims.quote: Average daily active users indicates the average number of people using Microsoft Copilot Chat per day over the selected period.

claims.claim: The report includes total prompts submitted.
claims.quote: Total prompts submitted refers to the overall number of prompts users sent to Microsoft Copilot Chat during the selected period.

claims.claim: The report includes average prompts submitted per user.
claims.quote: Average prompts submitted per user represents the mean number of prompts each active user sent to Microsoft Copilot Chat during the selected period.

claims.claim: The report offers a Summary view.
claims.quote: Summary view shows you the total usage of Microsoft Copilot Chat of the time frame.

claims.claim: The report offers a Trend view.
claims.quote: Trend view shows you the daily time trend of Microsoft Copilot Chat of the time frame.

claims.claim: The Trend view can be filtered by entry point.
claims.quote: When switching to Trend view, you can select one or multiple entry points in the dropdown list to see daily usage or compare among entry points.

claims.where: What's changing: entry points; Scope: Users
claims.claim: The report article lists Edge, Microsoft Copilot (app), Teams, Outlook, m365.cloud.microsoft/chat, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote as entry points.
claims.quote: The report currently supports only users without a Microsoft Copilot license who interact with Copilot Chat in Teams, Outlook, m365.cloud.microsoft/chat, Microsoft Copilot (app), Microsoft Edge, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.
claims.fix: After the entry-point list in Scope, add: 'This is the report article's general entry-point list, not a government-cloud availability list: Microsoft's service description says Copilot Chat is not available in the Edge sidebar in GCC, GCC High or DoD.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/office-365-platform-service-description/microsoft-365-copilot#feature-availability, which states: 'Microsoft Copilot Chat isn't available in the Edge sidebar for GCC/GCCH/DoD cloud environments.'

claims.where: Scope: Where; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The report is reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Reports > Microsoft Copilot > Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center. ... select Reports. ... Select Usage. ... On the Usage page, under Reports, select Microsoft Copilot, and then select Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: If Reports is not visible in the navigation, select Show all first.
claims.quote: If you don't see Reports, select Show all, and then select Reports.

claims.where: Scope: Where; Open questions: reporting window
claims.claim: The report article lists reporting periods of 7, 28, 90 or 180 days.
claims.quote: You can view the Microsoft Copilot Chat report over the last 7, 28, 90, or 180 days.

claims.claim: The overview lists 7, 30, 90 and 180 days, presented by the briefing as an unresolved reporting-window discrepancy.
claims.quote: Usage reports are generally available for the last 7, 30, 90, and 180 days. For details about specific report availability, see the individual usage report articles.
claims.fix: Remove the final Open questions bullet. The overview explicitly defers specific report availability to the individual article, so its general 30-day list does not require a correction before using the report article's documented 7, 28, 90 or 180-day periods.
